sources.title: Museo del Oro: Zenú
sources.note: Curatorial overview; sections La tradición Zenú, El sistema hidráulico and La importancia de la mujer. Original indexed text checked.

sources.title: Museo del Oro: Los zenúes y el manejo del medio ambiente (2010)
sources.note: Direct PDF, pages 9 to 10 and 28 (zero-based indices 8 to 9, 27). Educational reconstruction based on Plazas and Falchetti, not a contemporary eyewitness account.

sources.title: María M. Aguilera Díaz: La Mojana, riqueza natural y potencial económico
sources.note: Direct PDF read; printed pages 46, 48 and 50. Colonial narrative and archaeology synthesis.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Bird Staff Head, Zenú
sources.note: Direct collection record and technical commentary by Andrés A. Bustamante (2015); date 1 to 1000 CE. Collection object, no excavated findspot claimed.

sources.title: Artesanías de Colombia: Tejido en caña flecha
sources.note: Original indexed bilingual glossary; natural dyes, pictorial designs and approximately ten days to make a hat.

sources.title: Artesanías de Colombia: Tejeduría en Caña flecha, Resguardo Zenú (July 2025)
sources.note: Direct PDF; printed page 13, sections 5.2.3.3.1 and 5.2.3.3.2 on plantilla and encopadura.

sources.title: Ministerio de Cultura: Estudios Zenú
sources.note: Direct four-page ministry PDF. Page 2 explicitly attributes huru, home, to a community language coordinator; pages 1 to 3 distinguish older extinction claims from reported local knowledge and revitalization. Undated document, not evidence of preconquest orthography.

sources.title: DANE: Información sociodemográfica del pueblo Zenú (2022)
sources.note: Original indexed official report; contemporary population and caution that 2018 census language answers do not establish what respondents meant by native language.

sources.title: Sandra Leonor Cabrera Moreno: Cañari family names in the southern Andes (2025)
sources.note: Direct article read; abstract and introduction for core homeland and distinction between Cañari and Kichwa. Historical reconstructions elsewhere in article are not treated as certain.

sources.title: Antonio Fresco: El monumento incaico de Ingapirca y sus antecedentes cañaris
sources.note: INPC publication. Direct PDF fails; complete indexed original article text checked, especially La Condamine/La Vaguada, Pilaloma and earlier oval houses. Priestly-lineage interpretation not adopted as established.

sources.title: INPC: Ingapirca, un lugar para reencontrarnos con nuestras raíces (2020)
sources.note: Full original indexed article dated 13 January 2020; site museum, local history, Cañari occupation and Inca reorganization.

sources.title: INPC: Centro de Investigación e Interpretación Ingapirca
sources.note: Original indexed official PDF; Cañari occupation around 500 CE, later Inca complex, four hectares and road-network setting.

sources.title: INPC: Estudios multidisciplinarios, Hatun Cañar and colonial changes
sources.note: Direct PDF fails. Original indexed printed page 250 and preceding discussion of Inca population transfers checked. Query: "Estudiosmultidisciplinarios.pdf" "cañari".

sources.title: Gobierno Parroquial de Ingapirca: Cultura
sources.note: Direct local-government page; Vestimenta and Cultura Cañari on weaving and reciprocal work. Its conflation of ancient Cañari and Kichwa is not adopted.

sources.title: INPC: Mama Danza Cañari
sources.note: Full original indexed text checked; association with Corpus Christi, blended historical influences and two-file choreography.

sources.title: Luz Primogenita Alvacora Chima: Kichwa learning guide for Sisid school (2020)
sources.note: Direct PDF timed out. Original indexed printed page 37 gives Buenos días | Alli puncha and greeting exercise. Repository handle /123456789/18552 confirms author, January 2020 publication, Sisid seventh-grade context.

sources.title: Glottolog: Canari
sources.note: Direct scholarly language catalogue: ancient language extinct and primarily known through place names. Different from contemporary Kichwa.

sources.title: Municipio de Cañar: Con éxito concluyó el taller de kichwa
sources.note: Original indexed municipal report: 45 participants, hybrid online/in-person teaching by bilingual educator Andrés Quinde. No exact event year assigned because page access failed.

sources.title: CONAIE: Qué es la CONAIE? (2014)
sources.note: Full original indexed organizational statement lists Kañari among living highland Kichwa peoples and explains self-definition and organization.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Living people and related archaeological traditions, not one timeless empire. Imported 1492 to 1500 is coverage only.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded world-1492 polygon: longitude -76.6934 to -74.0617, latitude 7.6404 to 10.0279; Colombian Caribbean lowlands. Broad cultural extent does not certify a single state boundary.
batchIdentityNotes.language: Ministry testimony huru is carefully attributed; older blanket-extinction claims not repeated. No ancient readable inscription claimed.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Narrative scope is Ecuadorian Kañari homeland and continuity; ancient Cañari language distinguished from living Kichwa.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded world-1492 polygon spans longitude -79.7354 to -78.5150 and latitude -6.2880 to -2.1849. Southern reach includes northern Peru; imported outline cannot establish one continuous kingdom. Related Peruvian Kañaris identity/history not silently conflated.
batchIdentityNotes.dates: 1492 to 1500 map coverage. Narrative period breaks 1460/1530 approximate phase markers, not exact ethnic founding or disappearance dates.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: 2020 Sisid educational phrase Alli puncha, explicitly modern Kichwa; original indexed page 37. No manufactured ancient Cañari sentence.
